clue.text: Like fake news, a morass facing America

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the swamp word comes first

parts.note: a morass is a bog or swamp

explanation.surface: A jibe at fake news as a swamp that America is now up against.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake news is counterfeit and false, which is exactly what the slang adjective for sham describes.

clue.text: City powers relaxing blocks for solution

parts.note: Bath is an English city
cubes are third powers of numbers

explanation.surface: A city's authorities loosening their opposition to some plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' is a liquid: the blocks dissolve in water.
explanation.definitionFit: These fragrant tablets dissolve in bathwater to make a soothing soak.

clue.text: Developed expression of anger shortly before noon

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a growl is an angry sound

explanation.surface: Someone snapped irritably just before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Something developed has matured or increased in size.

clue.text: To drink or eat once more, stuffed head

parts.note: to sup is to sip a drink, and was formerly also to eat supper

indicators.note: stuffed suggests the letters are crammed in and messed up

explanation.surface: Someone takes another drink or a second helping, with a full belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the boss or person in overall charge.

clue.text: One in possession of advantage for tricks, the man had won

parts.note: a trump is the card suit that gives an advantage when taking tricks
one is the Roman numeral I
HE'D is the contraction of 'he had'

explanation.surface: A card player holding a trump card gets the better of the trick and wins.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of HE'D is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To have prevailed or come out on top is a straightforward synonym for having won.

clue.text: Spread French territory's name for a time

indicators.note: name for a time means one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia

clue.text: Republican finished supporting terror: he's not as bad as he was

definitions.text: he's not as bad as he was

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces support, or sit beneath, the first

parts.note: a terror is a naughty child, an imp
over means finished

explanation.surface: A political party member is done with backing terrorism.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting better is a reformed character, less bad than before.

clue.text: It could be generation of bulk manipulation

parts.note: mass means bulk
an age is a generation

explanation.surface: A musing on how a large quantity might be produced.

clue.text: Hospital treatment for bruises involves way of working instrument

parts.note: arnica is a herbal remedy for bruises
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

clue.text: Dull blue colour hiding feet

parts.note: blue means sad or down
a dye is a colour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding feet' removes the last letter from each word: N from the first, E from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowdy describes something drab and unfashionable.

clue.text: One will bring force, sort hippo out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to classify a hippopotamus, framed as a forceful arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel carrying soldiers brings a military force to where it is needed.

clue.text: Guard's son bragged loudly

crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast loudly

explanation.surface: A security guard's son was heard boasting at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard's' is 'Guard is'. In British slang a screw is a prison warder.

clue.text: Denounce Conservative-Democratic coalition at last

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word coalition

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a proposed alliance between Conservatives and Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to declare something wrong in public, a synonym for censure.

clue.text: Rhetoric of either a left-winger …?

parts.note: the ellipsis asks you to finish the sentence

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer (2,1,4) to complete 'either a left-winger ...': the missing alternative is a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of public speaking and persuasive eloquence is another name for rhetoric.

clue.text: Large canine almost cut with teeth seizing grainy pasta

almost means the word is cut short of its final letter

orzo is a small rice-shaped pasta

explanation.definitionFit: This Russian wolfhound is a large breed of dog.

clue.text: Misleading or guile is based on belief

indicators.note: misleading suggests the letters are led astray into a new order

clue.text: Electromechanical engineers phone for the purposes of repairs

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: Engineers ring in about getting something fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army corps that maintains and repairs equipment.

clue.text: House of aged cavalryman across a street

parts.note: a lancer was an old-time cavalry soldier with a lance

explanation.surface: An old cavalry officer's home stands across the road.

explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty of England whose emblem was the red rose.

clue.text: Cold as a dish brought to table a second time

definitions.meaning: cold here means aloof or standoffish

definitions.text: as a dish brought to table a second time
definitions.meaning: food put out again for diners has been served once more

explanation.surface: A dish of leftovers coming back out from the kitchen, now cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means distant in manner; split as re-served, it means dished up again.

clue.text: Bolt, maybe turning one right to left produces a sharp fragment

indicators.note: turning one letter into another means swapping a single letter

parts.note: Usain Bolt is an example of a sprinter

explanation.surface: A runner like Bolt swerving from the right lane to the left ends with a sharp shard.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter is a thin sharp piece broken off wood or glass.

clue.text: Selflessness ideally without boundaries, invariant somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the remaining letters are arranged some other way
without boundaries means the first and last letters are removed

clue.text: Get in boat, tossing

indicators.note: tossing suggests the letters are thrown about like a boat on waves

explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to acquire or come by it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: British Caucasian bringing up one metalworker

one is the Roman numeral I

clue.text: Oddly padded, it could be fortuitous yet uncalled-for

indicators.note: padding the word out with odd letters gives the following words, so take their even letters

explanation.surface: A chance remark, oddly stuffed out, may be fortunate yet unnecessary.

clue.text: Camper van covered in seaweed etc somewhere around Faro

parts.note: algae include seaweeds and similar simple plants

explanation.surface: A campervan smothered in seaweed somewhere on a coastal holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Faro is the main city and airport of Portugal's southern holiday coast.

clue.text: Sponge underlying aluminium disc

indicators.note: in a down clue underlying puts this piece below the other

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
to bum is to sponge or scrounge

clue.text: Cargo for extra-cheap air passage

clue.text: Book with Hellenic character showing all the life in a place

definitions.text: all the life in a place

parts.note: iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A volume featuring a Greek figure that captures every living thing somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use this term for the flora and fauna of a region taken together.

clue.text: Drive badly as request for noise-reduction added to stopping distance

clue.text: Perhaps Jack said one gets 'edgy' in a strop

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike
